parameter_provenance.objective: Make off-axis force and section torque observable in a stable free-space mechanics fixture while preserving exact force and generalized-torque balance.
parameter_provenance.uncertainty: No value in this section is a measured L1 torsional stiffness, inertia, pressure, damping, CSA, Fmax, or force in newtons.

required_gates: every active load traces to an earlier named motor-neuron spike
each muscle contributes exactly two off-axis endpoint applications
free-space net internal force is numerical zero
free-space generalized internal torque is numerical zero
centerline-only moment is nonzero and exactly canceled by section torque
left and right loads are mirror covariant
equal bilateral activation produces no differential load
attachment lesion preserves upstream activation and removes mechanics
material frames remain right-handed and orthonormal
the frozen named-fiber steering v1 artifact remains unchanged
validation.claim_limit: Reduced oriented-section mechanics reference with anatomy-derived normalized attachments and model-fitted angular parameters; not measured L1 material mechanics, not a full shell/continuum, and not yet a contact-integrated locomotion validation.

limitations: The section tangent is constrained to the centerline; shear and cross-section warping are not resolved.
Only twist about the tangent is an independent rotational degree of freedom; bending is carried by centerline particles.
The fixture runs in free space and cannot demonstrate locomotion or steering without environmental reaction forces.
Normalized attachment coordinates remain anatomy-derived hypotheses rather than measured L1 3D coordinates.
All force and torque magnitudes use model units, not newtons or newton-metres.
Pressure, anisotropic cuticle elasticity, self-contact, and substrate traction remain future work.
